newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Lawyers for government say Bhutto not under arrest.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers for government say Bhutto not under arrest.

text.p: Lawyers for Pakistan's caretaker government told a court on Wednesday that sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto was not under arrest.
They were responding to a habeas corpus petition filed on Tuesday by lawyers for former defence minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani pleading that Bhutto had been "held unlawfully incommunicado".

"It is vehemently denied that the former Prime Minister is under arrest," the lawyers for the caretaker government told the court in Rawalpindi, near Islamabad. (A) Police contingent is deployed for (the) personal safety of the former prime minister."
They called for Meerani's petition to be rejected. The court was then adjourned.
Bhutto was sacked on Tuesday for a second time in her turbulent political career by the country's president, who accused her beleaguered government of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
She has remained a virtual prisoner in her official Islamabad residence but has been allowed to meet party colleagues and take telephone calls, a government official said on Wednesday.
"She met three or four party colleagues last night and received calls from former ministers," the official said, adding that restrictions on Bhutto might be lifted within a day.

There has been no official word on Bhutto's status, but she has not been allowed to leave the prime minister's elegant house on a hill overlooking Islamabad and police guarding the gate turned away many others who tried to visit her on Tuesday.
